html:
The Aluku, also called the Boni, are a Maroon people of French Guiana, descended from Africans who escaped the plantations of Suriname in the 1700s. They live mainly along the upper Maroni River, around Maripasoula and Papaïchton.

Their name Boni comes from Boni, a leader who fought the Dutch colonial army and its allies in the Boni Wars of the 1770s and 1780s. Pressed hard, the group crossed the Maroni River into French territory, where they rebuilt their villages. Boni was killed in 1793. Like the Saramaka and other Maroons of Suriname, they kept a culture rooted in West Africa, with their own creole language, religion and wood carving.

They lived largely apart until the 1900s. Today many Aluku have moved to the coast and to French Guiana's towns, where they make up a large part of the people of the west.
